findings.title: Keep the React UI message in its supported interpolation format
findings.body: This changes the account UI message from i18next's `{{0}}` interpolation syntax to Java MessageFormat placeholders and a `choice` expression. The React UI does not evaluate Java MessageFormat, so multivalued-size validation errors will display literal placeholders and the choice expression instead of the attribute name and limits. The same regression is introduced in the admin UI's messages_en.properties at line 3138. Keep these frontend resources in the frontend's supported format.

findings.title: Use Lithuanian rather than Italian for the OTP instruction
findings.body: The replacement for `loginTotpStep1` is Italian (`Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare`), although this is the Lithuanian message bundle. Lithuanian users will now receive an untranslated OTP setup instruction in another language. The same incorrect replacement appears in the Lithuanian account bundle's `totpStep1` at line 101; both should contain Lithuanian instructions.

findings.title: Validate HTML inside choice branches instead of discarding them
findings.body: Normalization replaces the entire choice expression with `...` before HTML validation for the expiration-unit and multivalued-size messages. Consequently, a translation such as `{0,choice,0#<script>alert(1)</script>|1#second|1<seconds}` passes verification because its malicious HTML is removed from the verifier's input, while the original resource remains unchanged and MessageFormat can emit that branch at runtime. Only exempt the choice syntax itself, or validate each branch's contents, so these messages cannot bypass the new HTML check.
